title: The Coach’s night. A familiar opponent.
summary: Chicago’s first home game after Mike Ditka’s death brought New England to Soldier Field—the same opponent his Bears beat in Super Bowl XX. The Bears honored him before a 30–24 win.

timeline.label: October 9
timeline.text: Ditka died at age 86. He had been a Hall of Fame tight end and Chicago’s Super Bowl-winning head coach.

timeline.label: October 22 · Before kickoff
timeline.text: Soldier Field held a moment of silence. Commemorative No. 89 markings and jersey patches accompanied fan tributes and stick-on mustaches.

timeline.label: The opponent
timeline.text: New England was also Chicago’s opponent in Super Bowl XX, which Ditka’s Bears won 46–10 following the 1985 season.

timeline.label: Final whistle
timeline.text: Chicago won 30–24. The tribute and the victory are documented; their coexistence does not measure an emotional effect on performance.

unusual: The first home tribute paired Ditka’s team with the opponent from his defining championship. That historical echo gives the evening significance beyond an ordinary Thursday game.
explanations: A scheduled matchup became a meaningful memorial occasion. Team emotion may be part of the human story, but one result cannot isolate its effect from football factors or establish a repeatable betting pattern.
questions: How much did the tribute affect performance? No causal measurement or comparable-game study is available here.
